1→"""Single-batch Sobol design generator for the T3-prism BO campaign.
  2→
  3→Per PR #35 comment 4503109338 from @sgbaird (carried over from PR #30 / PR #24):
  4→this is a **single-iteration**, human-in-the-loop, T3-prism-only first batch.
  5→No measured objectives are reported back; this only emits the initial Sobol
  6→quasi-random design set, renders each specimen, packs them onto a single
  7→Bambu H2D build plate, and writes a preview PNG so the team can spot-check
  8→before opening the result in Bambu Studio.
  9→
 10→This is a *restricted* adaptation of ``bo/tensegrity_campaign.py`` from
 11→``copilot/scaffold-bayesian-optimization-script`` (the PR #30 / #24 scaffold).
 12→The full search space there spans every topology, tiling, material pairing,
 13→and build orientation in the project's Edison-curated literature table. Here
 14→we deliberately freeze every variable that is *not* specific to the T3-prism
 15→geometry, since the team has only confirmed printability for T3-prisms so
 16→far (PRs #30 / #24 / #16 / #35).
 17→
 18→Frozen (defaults match the production target on this branch):
 19→
 20→* ``topology`` = ``"t3_prism"``  -- canonical 3-strut tensegrity.
 21→* ``tiling`` = ``"1x1x1"``       -- single unit cell.
 22→* ``struts_per_cell`` = 3        -- T3 by definition.
 23→* ``build_orientation`` = ``"vertical"`` -- per the comment, "Vertically
 24→  orient it so you can maximize the number on the build plate".
 25→* Materials: PLA struts + TPU 85A cables on the Bambu H2D IDEX nozzles
 26→  (same as ``slices/t3-prism.H2D-MM-PLAstruts-TPUcables.3mf``).
 27→* Supports: OFF in the slicer. Per the comment, "@achris0520 will manually
 28→  paint on supports, so you can leave those off"; the modeled-in PLA
 29→  scaffold pillars from PR #35 commit 5437366 are likewise disabled here
 30→  (``part="all"`` in the SCAD, no ``scaffold`` block).
 31→
 32→Sweep (T3-prism-specific geometric variables, taken from
 33→``cad/t3-prism/t3-prism.scad``):
 34→
 35→================================  ==================  =====================
 36→Variable                          Range (mm/deg)      Maps to SCAD parameter
 37→================================  ==================  =====================
 38→``R_mm``       (radius)             [25, 40]          ``R_base``
 39→``H_mm``       (height)             [60, 110]         ``H_base``
 40→``twist_deg``  (top-vs-bottom)      [40, 80]          ``twist``
 41→``strut_d_mm`` (PLA strut Ø)        [6.0, 12.0]       ``strut_d_base``
 42→``cable_d_mm`` (TPU cable Ø)        [3.0, 5.5]        ``cable_d_base``
 43→================================  ==================  =====================
 44→
 45→The cable_d lower bound (3.0 mm) sits above the Bambu auto-support detector
 46→threshold @achris0520 hit empirically at scale 1.3x (cable_d ≈ 3.9 mm) and
 47→matches Edison ANALYSIS ``25c1c897``'s recommended floor (3.0–4.0 mm) so even
 48→the smallest cable in the batch will TPU-self-bridge without painted
 49→supports failing mid-print.
 50→
 51→Output files (next to this script):
 52→
 53→* ``t3-prism-bo-batch.csv``                                       -- one row per specimen + frozen vars
 54→* ``t3-prism-bo-batch.json``                                      -- same data + Ax client snapshot
 55→* ``t3-prism-bo-batch.scad``                                      -- generated OpenSCAD wrapper
 56→* ``t3-prism-bo-batch.stl``                                       -- packed-on-plate combined STL (all parts fused)
 57→* ``t3-prism-bo-batch-struts.stl``                                -- struts + joint spheres only (extruder 1 / PLA)
 58→* ``t3-prism-bo-batch-cables.stl``                                -- cables only (extruder 2 / TPU)
 59→* ``t3-prism-bo-batch-plate.png``                                 -- top-down build-plate preview PNG
 60→* ``t3-prism-bo-batch-iso.png``                                   -- iso preview PNG
 61→* ``slices/t3-prism-bo-batch.H2D-MM-PLAstruts-TPUcables.3mf``     -- Bambu H2D MM project (struts/PLA + cables/TPU,
 62→                                                                     re-importable into Bambu Studio with
 63→                                                                     per-part extruder assignment; *no* supports —
 64→                                                                     paint them on manually per @achris0520's tip
 65→                                                                     in PR #35 comment 4502140147)
 66→
 67→Run::
 68→
 69→    pip install ax-platform numpy
 70→    sudo apt-get install -y openscad admesh xvfb \\
 71→        gstreamer1.0-plugins-base libsoup-3.0-0 libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0
 72→    python3 bo/t3_prism_sobol_batch.py
 73→"""
 74→
 75→from __future__ import annotations
 76→
 77→import argparse
 78→import csv
 79→import json
 80→import logging
 81→import math
 82→import shutil
 83→import subprocess
 84→import sys
 85→from pathlib import Path
 86→
 87→from ax.service.ax_client import AxClient, ObjectiveProperties
 88→
 89→logging.getLogger("ax").setLevel(logging.WARNING)
 90→
 91→# ---- Frozen experimental context -------------------------------------------
 92→TOPOLOGY = "t3_prism"
 93→TILING = "1x1x1"
 94→STRUTS_PER_CELL = 3
 95→BUILD_ORIENTATION = "vertical"
 96→TPU_SHORE = "85A"          # NinjaFlex-class; lab default
 97→STRUT_MATERIAL = "PLA"     # Bambu PLA Basic on extruder 1
 98→CABLE_MATERIAL = "TPU"     # Bambu TPU 85A on extruder 2
 99→SUPPORTS = "manual_painted"  # Audrey paints them on in Bambu Studio
100→JOINT_D_BASE = 7.0         # mm, kept fixed (t3-prism.scad default)
101→
102→# ---- Build-plate geometry (Bambu Lab H2D) ----------------------------------
103→PLATE_X = 350.0  # mm
104→PLATE_Y = 320.0  # mm
105→PLATE_MARGIN = 5.0  # keep specimens off the edge
106→# Reserve a strip on the +X side of the plate for the IDEX prime / flush
107→# tower that the slicer drops in for PLA<->TPU material changes.
108→# Bambu Studio's default prime tower is ~50 mm square; reserving a 50 mm
109→# wide × full-Y strip on +X gives the slicer ample room to drop the tower
110→# without colliding with any specimen corner (PR #35 comment 4513445377).
111→PRIME_TOWER_RESERVE_X = 50.0
112→
113→# ---- Sobol batch knobs -----------------------------------------------------
114→# 9 specimens packed 3x3 on the H2D plate. PR #35 comment 4513164299
115→# briefly dropped this to 6 (3x2) to make room for an extra-fat 70 mm
116→# prime-tower reserve, but PR #35 comment 4513445377 reverted to 3x3 with
117→# a smaller 50 mm tower reserve and a 6 mm inter-cell air gap (up from
118→# the original 2 mm that was "too tight last time" per comment
119→# 4513164299, but tighter than the temporary 12 mm used at n=6 so 3x3
120→# still fits inside the prime-tower-reduced 290x310 mm usable area).
121→N_SPECIMENS = 9      # 3 rows x 3 cols
122→SEED = 0
123→
124→# ---- Search space (T3-prism-specific geometric variables only) -------------
125→# Bounds reconciled against:
126→#   * cad/t3-prism/t3-prism.scad's existing defaults at scale_factor=1.5
127→#     (R=37.5, H=105, strut_d=9, cable_d=4.5).
128→#   * PR #24 Edison literature table 5ae24eaf (strut_d 1.5-5 mm pre-scale,
129→#     L/D in [8,25], cable_d 1.0-3.0 mm pre-scale, twist 10-45 deg).
130→#   * PR #35 print history: cable_d >= 3.0 mm is required for the top-cable
131→#     bridge to survive without auto-supports failing.
132→PARAMETERS: list[dict] = [
133→    {"name": "R_mm",        "type": "range", "bounds": [25.0,  40.0], "value_type": "float"},
134→    {"name": "H_mm",        "type": "range", "bounds": [60.0, 110.0], "value_type": "float"},
135→    {"name": "twist_deg",   "type": "range", "bounds": [40.0,  80.0], "value_type": "float"},
136→    {"name": "strut_d_mm",  "type": "range", "bounds": [ 6.0,  12.0], "value_type": "float"},
137→    {"name": "cable_d_mm",  "type": "range", "bounds": [ 3.0,   5.5], "value_type": "float"},
138→]
139→
140→
141→def specimen_footprint(r_mm: float, strut_d_mm: float, joint_d_mm: float = JOINT_D_BASE,
142→                       cable_d_mm: float = 0.0) -> float:
143→    """Bounding box edge length (mm) for one specimen.
144→
145→    A T3-prism's triangular caps inscribe in a circle of radius R; the
146→    outermost geometry is the captive-core joint shell at each corner, so
147→    the bounding diameter is ``2R + shell_od`` (with ``shell_od`` derived
148→    the same way the SCAD template does it — see ``SPECIMEN_TEMPLATE``).
149→    Strut/cable cylinders fall *inside* this circle (they connect corners)
150→    so they do not extend the footprint.
151→    """
152→    del strut_d_mm  # kept for backwards-compatible signature
153→    if cable_d_mm > 0:
154→        # Mirror the captive-core SCAD: bore = cable_d (zero clearance —
155→        # TPU fills bore exactly, bonded), core_od = max(bore+3, joint_d),
156→        # shell_id = core_od (TPU core touches PLA — bonded), shell_od =
157→        # max(shell_id+3.2, joint_d). PR #35 comment 4513722886.
158→        bore_d = cable_d_mm
159→        core_od = max(bore_d + 2 * 1.5, joint_d_mm)
160→        shell_id = core_od
161→        shell_od = max(shell_id + 2 * 1.6, joint_d_mm)
162→    else:
163→        shell_od = joint_d_mm
164→    return 2.0 * r_mm + shell_od
165→
166→
167→def grid_layout(n: int, footprints: list[float]) -> tuple[int, int, float, float]:
168→    """Choose a rows x cols grid that fits on the plate.
169→
170→    Returns (n_rows, n_cols, cell_x, cell_y). Cell dimensions are sized to
171→    the worst-case specimen footprint plus a small air gap; specimens that
172→    are smaller than the worst case still benefit from the tight pack since
173→    we keep the grid square.
174→
175→    Honours ``PRIME_TOWER_RESERVE_X`` — the +X strip is unavailable, so we
176→    prefer layouts that are taller than they are wide.
177→    """
178→    # 6 mm air gap restores breathing room between specimen bounding
179→    # circles (the previous 2 mm gap from PR #35 comment 4503427854 was
180→    # "too tight last time" per PR #35 comment 4513164299) while still
181→    # allowing 3x3 packing to fit inside the prime-tower-reduced usable
182→    # area (PR #35 comment 4513445377).
183→    air_gap = 6.0
184→    cell = max(footprints) + air_gap
185→    usable_x = PLATE_X - 2 * PLATE_MARGIN - PRIME_TOWER_RESERVE_X
186→    usable_y = PLATE_Y - 2 * PLATE_MARGIN
187→    # Prefer the most square-ish layout that *fits*. Sweep candidate column
188→    # counts from 1..n; for each, derive rows = ceil(n/cols), check both
189→    # dimensions, score by "squareness" (smaller |rows-cols|).
190→    best: tuple[int, int] | None = None
191→    best_score = math.inf
192→    for cols in range(1, n + 1):
193→        rows = math.ceil(n / cols)
194→        if cols * cell > usable_x or rows * cell > usable_y:
195→            continue
196→        score = abs(rows - cols) + 0.01 * (rows * cols - n)  # tie-break: fewer empty cells
197→        if score < best_score:
198→            best_score = score
199→            best = (rows, cols)
200→    if best is None:
201→        # Fall back to original square-ish grid; caller will print a warning.
202→        cols = math.ceil(math.sqrt(n))
203→        rows = math.ceil(n / cols)
204→        best = (rows, cols)
205→    rows, cols = best
206→    return rows, cols, cell, cell
207→
208→
209→SPECIMEN_TEMPLATE = """\
210→// specimen {idx:02d}  R={R:.2f} H={H:.2f} twist={tw:.2f} strut_d={sd:.2f} cable_d={cd:.2f}
211→// Captive-core joint params (mirror cad/t3-prism/t3-prism.scad,
212→// PR #35 comment 4513722886 + 4514072758): bore = cable_d (zero
213→// clearance — TPU fills the bore exactly); core_od >= bore + 2*1.5
214→// mm so the captive TPU mass cannot back out the bore; shell_id =
215→// core_od (TPU core touches PLA inner wall — bonded joint); shell_od =
216→// shell_id + 2*1.6 mm PLA wall (lifted to >= joint_d so the joint is
217→// never smaller than the legacy design). The shell uses a teardrop
218→// hull blend toward the strut axis (PR #35 comment 4514072758 — "the
219→// teardrop shape was fine"), and cable bores are OUTWARD-ONLY so they
220→// don't punch holes through the opposite side of the shell.
221→S{idx:02d}_BORE_D    = {cd:.4f};
222→S{idx:02d}_CORE_OD   = max(S{idx:02d}_BORE_D + 2*1.5, {jd:.4f});
223→S{idx:02d}_SHELL_ID  = S{idx:02d}_CORE_OD;
224→S{idx:02d}_SHELL_OD  = max(S{idx:02d}_SHELL_ID + 2*1.6, {jd:.4f});
225→S{idx:02d}_TEARDROP_Z = 1.5;
226→S{idx:02d}_TEARDROP_D = {sd:.4f} * 1.10;
227→module specimen_{idx:02d}_member(p1, p2, d) {{
228→    v=p2-p1; L=norm(v);
229→    yaw=atan2(v[1],v[0]);
230→    pitch=atan2(sqrt(v[0]*v[0]+v[1]*v[1]),v[2]);
231→    translate(p1) rotate([0,0,yaw]) rotate([0,pitch,0]) {{
232→        cylinder(h=L,d=d); sphere(d=d); translate([0,0,L]) sphere(d=d);
233→    }}
234→}}
235→module specimen_{idx:02d}_bore(dir, d, len) {{
236→    // Outward-only bore (see cad/t3-prism/t3-prism.scad bore_along() —
237→    // the previous centred bore punched holes through both sides of
238→    // the shell, PR #35 comment 4514072758).
239→    yaw=atan2(dir[1],dir[0]);
240→    pitch=atan2(sqrt(dir[0]*dir[0]+dir[1]*dir[1]),dir[2]);
241→    rotate([0,0,yaw]) rotate([0,pitch,0]) translate([0,0,-0.5])
242→        cylinder(h=len + 0.5, d=d);
243→}}
244→function specimen_{idx:02d}_bp(i) = [{R:.4f}*cos(90+120*i), {R:.4f}*sin(90+120*i), 0];
245→function specimen_{idx:02d}_tp(i) = [{R:.4f}*cos(90+120*i+{tw:.4f}),
246→                                     {R:.4f}*sin(90+120*i+{tw:.4f}), {H:.4f}];
247→function specimen_{idx:02d}_unit(v) = v / norm(v);
248→function specimen_{idx:02d}_sdir_b(i) =
249→    specimen_{idx:02d}_unit(specimen_{idx:02d}_tp(i) - specimen_{idx:02d}_bp(i));
250→function specimen_{idx:02d}_sdir_t(i) =
251→    specimen_{idx:02d}_unit(specimen_{idx:02d}_bp(i) - specimen_{idx:02d}_tp(i));
252→function specimen_{idx:02d}_cdirs_b(i) = [
253→    specimen_{idx:02d}_unit(specimen_{idx:02d}_bp((i+1)%3) - specimen_{idx:02d}_bp(i)),
254→    specimen_{idx:02d}_unit(specimen_{idx:02d}_bp((i+2)%3) - specimen_{idx:02d}_bp(i)),
255→    specimen_{idx:02d}_unit(specimen_{idx:02d}_tp((i+2)%3) - specimen_{idx:02d}_bp(i)),
256→];
257→function specimen_{idx:02d}_cdirs_t(i) = [
258→    specimen_{idx:02d}_unit(specimen_{idx:02d}_tp((i+1)%3) - specimen_{idx:02d}_tp(i)),
259→    specimen_{idx:02d}_unit(specimen_{idx:02d}_tp((i+2)%3) - specimen_{idx:02d}_tp(i)),
260→    specimen_{idx:02d}_unit(specimen_{idx:02d}_bp((i+1)%3) - specimen_{idx:02d}_tp(i)),
261→];
262→module specimen_{idx:02d}_shell(V, sdir, cdirs) {{
263→    translate(V) difference() {{
264→        // Teardrop hull blend toward the strut axis (PR #35 comment
265→        // 4514072758 — "the teardrop shape was fine"). The strut
266→        // emerges from the bump, not through a punched hole.
267→        hull() {{
268→            sphere(d=S{idx:02d}_SHELL_OD);
269→            translate(sdir * (S{idx:02d}_SHELL_OD/2 + S{idx:02d}_TEARDROP_Z))
270→                sphere(d=S{idx:02d}_TEARDROP_D);
271→        }}
272→        sphere(d=S{idx:02d}_SHELL_ID);
273→        for (cd = cdirs)
274→            specimen_{idx:02d}_bore(cd, S{idx:02d}_BORE_D, S{idx:02d}_SHELL_OD);
275→    }}
276→}}
277→module specimen_{idx:02d}_struts() {{
278→    union() {{
279→        for (i=[0:2]) {{
280→            specimen_{idx:02d}_shell(specimen_{idx:02d}_bp(i),
281→                                     specimen_{idx:02d}_sdir_b(i),
282→                                     specimen_{idx:02d}_cdirs_b(i));
283→            specimen_{idx:02d}_shell(specimen_{idx:02d}_tp(i),
284→                                     specimen_{idx:02d}_sdir_t(i),
285→                                     specimen_{idx:02d}_cdirs_t(i));
286→            specimen_{idx:02d}_member(specimen_{idx:02d}_bp(i),
287→                                     specimen_{idx:02d}_tp(i), {sd:.4f});
288→        }}
289→    }}
290→}}
291→module specimen_{idx:02d}_cables() {{
292→    union() {{
293→        for (i=[0:2]) {{
294→            specimen_{idx:02d}_member(specimen_{idx:02d}_bp(i),
295→                                     specimen_{idx:02d}_bp((i+1)%3), {cd:.4f});
296→            specimen_{idx:02d}_member(specimen_{idx:02d}_tp(i),
297→                                     specimen_{idx:02d}_tp((i+1)%3), {cd:.4f});
298→            specimen_{idx:02d}_member(specimen_{idx:02d}_bp((i+1)%3),
299→                                     specimen_{idx:02d}_tp(i),       {cd:.4f});
300→            // Captive TPU cores inside each PLA shell cavity.
301→            translate(specimen_{idx:02d}_bp(i)) sphere(d=S{idx:02d}_CORE_OD);
302→            translate(specimen_{idx:02d}_tp(i)) sphere(d=S{idx:02d}_CORE_OD);
303→        }}
304→        // Bounding-box z-anchor so cables.stl inherits the struts.stl
305→        // world-Z extents (fixes the "cables too low" misalignment;
306→        // see cad/t3-prism/t3-prism.scad cables_z_anchor()).
307→        translate([0, 0, -S{idx:02d}_SHELL_OD/2])
308→            cube([0.005, 0.005, {H:.4f} + S{idx:02d}_SHELL_OD], center=false);
309→    }}
310→}}
311→module specimen_{idx:02d}() {{
312→    if      (part == "struts") specimen_{idx:02d}_struts();
313→    else if (part == "cables") specimen_{idx:02d}_cables();
314→    else union() {{ specimen_{idx:02d}_struts(); specimen_{idx:02d}_cables(); }}
315→}}
316→if (spec == -1 || spec == {idx})
317→    translate([{cx:.3f}, {cy:.3f}, {cz:.3f}]) specimen_{idx:02d}();
318→"""
319→

321→def emit_specimen_scad(idx: int, params: dict, cx: float, cy: float, cz: float) -> str:
322→    """SCAD snippet that instantiates one specimen at the given plate coords.
323→
324→    Each specimen is wrapped in its own module so $fn / variable shadowing
325→    cannot leak across specimens in the unioned plate file.
326→    """
327→    return SPECIMEN_TEMPLATE.format(
328→        idx=idx,
329→        R=params["R_mm"], H=params["H_mm"], tw=params["twist_deg"],
330→        sd=params["strut_d_mm"], cd=params["cable_d_mm"], jd=JOINT_D_BASE,
331→        cx=cx, cy=cy, cz=cz,
332→    )

334→
335→def write_batch_scad(path: Path, specimens: list[dict], rows: int, cols: int,
336→                     cell_x: float, cell_y: float) -> None:
337→    """Write the OpenSCAD wrapper that unions all specimens onto one plate."""
338→    # Centre the grid on the *usable* portion of the plate (i.e. the plate
339→    # minus the +X strip reserved for the IDEX prime/flush tower, per
340→    # PR #35 comment 4513164299).
341→    grid_w = cols * cell_x
342→    grid_h = rows * cell_y
343→    usable_x = PLATE_X - PRIME_TOWER_RESERVE_X
344→    x0 = (usable_x - grid_w) / 2.0 + cell_x / 2.0
345→    y0 = (PLATE_Y - grid_h) / 2.0 + cell_y / 2.0
346→    # Lift each specimen so the bottom of every captive-core PLA shell sits
347→    # at the build plate (matches Bambu's auto-bed-placement). The captive
348→    # shell OD is the larger of (cable_d + 5.4 mm) and JOINT_D_BASE, so the
349→    # bottom-vertex shell underside is at SCAD z = -shell_od/2 ≤ -joint_d/2.
350→    # Use the worst-case (largest shell_od across the batch) so EVERY
351→    # specimen's shell underside lands on or below the bed.
352→    max_cable_d = max(s["cable_d_mm"] for s in specimens)
353→    max_shell_od = max(max_cable_d + 2*1.5 + 2*1.6, JOINT_D_BASE)
354→    z_lift = max_shell_od / 2.0
355→    parts: list[str] = []
356→    parts.append(
357→        "// AUTO-GENERATED by bo/t3_prism_sobol_batch.py — do not hand-edit.\n"
358→        "// Single-batch Sobol design set for the T3-prism BO campaign\n"
359→        "// (PR #35 comment 4503109338). All specimens vertically oriented\n"
360→        "// (load axis = z). Supports will be manually painted in Bambu\n"
361→        "// Studio per @achris0520's tip in PR #35 comment 4502140147.\n"
362→        f"// Plate: {PLATE_X:.0f} x {PLATE_Y:.0f} mm (Bambu Lab H2D).\n"
363→        f"// Grid : {rows} x {cols} (cell {cell_x:.1f} x {cell_y:.1f} mm).\n"
364→        "//\n"
365→        "// `part` selects which half of each specimen to emit, mirroring\n"
366→        "// `cad/t3-prism/t3-prism.scad`:\n"
367→        "//   \"all\"    -> struts + cables fused (preview / single-material)\n"
368→        "//   \"struts\" -> rigid skeleton + joint spheres (PLA / extruder 1)\n"
369→        "//   \"cables\" -> tension members only (TPU / extruder 2)\n"
370→        "// Override at the CLI with `-D 'part=\"struts\"'`.\n"
371→        "part = \"all\";  // \"all\" | \"struts\" | \"cables\"\n"
372→        "// `spec` filters which specimen to emit; -1 (default) emits all\n"
373→        "// of them on the plate. Per-specimen STLs are rendered by the\n"
374→        "// driver with `-D spec=N` (PR #35 comment 4513722886): the\n"
375→        "// resulting per-specimen pair of struts/cables STLs is what\n"
376→        "// lets BambuStudio --assemble produce one composite object per\n"
377→        "// specimen instead of one giant fused object.\n"
378→        "spec = -1;\n"
379→        "\n"
380→    )
381→    for idx, params in enumerate(specimens):
382→        col = idx % cols
383→        row = idx // cols
384→        cx = x0 + col * cell_x
385→        cy = y0 + row * cell_y
386→        parts.append(emit_specimen_scad(idx, params, cx, cy, z_lift))
387→    # Render a thin visual marker for the reserved prime/flush-tower zone
388→    # (rendered only when ``part == "all"`` so it never leaks into the
389→    # struts/cables STLs the slicer assembles into the H2D MM .3mf).
390→    pt_x = PRIME_TOWER_RESERVE_X - 2 * PLATE_MARGIN
391→    parts.append(
392→        f"\n// Visual marker for the IDEX prime/flush-tower reserve zone.\n"
393→        f"// {PRIME_TOWER_RESERVE_X:.0f} mm wide strip on the +X side of the\n"
394→        f"// plate is held back from the specimen grid so the slicer can\n"
395→        f"// drop a wipe tower there without colliding (PR #35 comment\n"
396→        f"// 4513164299).\n"
397→        f"if (spec == -1 && part == \"all\") {{\n"
398→        f"  translate([{PLATE_X - PRIME_TOWER_RESERVE_X + PLATE_MARGIN:.2f}, "
399→        f"{PLATE_MARGIN:.2f}, 0])\n"
400→        f"    cube([{pt_x:.2f}, {PLATE_Y - 2 * PLATE_MARGIN:.2f}, 0.2]);\n"
401→        f"}}\n"
402→    )
403→    path.write_text("".join(parts))

406→def run_openscad(scad: Path, out: Path, *, camera: str | None = None,
407→                 image_size: str | None = None, defines: dict | None = None) -> None:
408→    """Invoke OpenSCAD headlessly via xvfb-run, writing STL or PNG."""
409→    cmd = ["xvfb-run", "-a", "openscad", "-o", str(out)]
410→    if out.suffix == ".stl":
411→        cmd += ["--export-format=binstl"]
412→    if camera:
413→        cmd += [f"--camera={camera}"]
414→    if image_size:
415→        cmd += [f"--imgsize={image_size}"]
416→    for k, v in (defines or {}).items():
417→        if isinstance(v, str):
418→            cmd += ["-D", f'{k}="{v}"']
419→        else:
420→            cmd += ["-D", f"{k}={v}"]
421→    cmd += [str(scad)]
422→    subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)

475→def _split_assembled_into_objects(
476→    proj_3mf: Path, pairs: list[tuple[str, str]]
477→) -> None:
478→    """Split the single composite object emitted by ``--assemble`` into one
479→    composite object per (struts_stl, cables_stl) pair.
480→
481→    Per PR #35 comment 4513722886 (@sgbaird), each tensegrity iteration on
482→    the plate must be its own Bambu Studio object made up of two part
483→    groups (PLA struts + TPU cables) so it can be moved as a unit. The
484→    BambuStudio CLI's ``--assemble`` flag instead merges *all* passed STLs
485→    into a single composite object, so the team can't move one specimen
486→    independently of the others without lassoing both of its parts.
487→
488→    Fix: after ``--assemble``, edit ``3D/3dmodel.model`` and
489→    ``Metadata/model_settings.config`` in-place to split the single
490→    composite object into ``len(pairs)`` composite objects, each
491→    referencing two of the per-specimen STL meshes (struts → extruder 1,
492→    cables → extruder 2). The underlying ``3D/Objects/object_1.model``
493→    mesh data is untouched; only the grouping changes.
494→    """
495→    import re
496→    import uuid
497→    import zipfile
498→
499→    MODEL_PATH = "3D/3dmodel.model"
500→    CFG_PATH = "Metadata/model_settings.config"
501→
502→    # Mapping from STL filename -> (specimen_index, extruder_id). Struts
503→    # always go to extruder 1, cables to extruder 2.
504→    name_to_spec: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] = {}
505→    for spec_idx, (struts_name, cables_name) in enumerate(pairs):
506→        name_to_spec[struts_name] = (spec_idx, 1)
507→        name_to_spec[cables_name] = (spec_idx, 2)
508→
509→    with zipfile.ZipFile(proj_3mf, "r") as zin:
510→        infos = zin.infolist()
511→        contents = {info.filename: zin.read(info.filename) for info in infos}
512→
513→    if MODEL_PATH not in contents:
514→        raise RuntimeError(f"{proj_3mf}: missing {MODEL_PATH}")
515→    if CFG_PATH not in contents:
516→        raise RuntimeError(f"{proj_3mf}: missing {CFG_PATH}")
517→
518→    # ---- Patch model_settings.config first (we need part-name -> id mapping). ----
519→    cfg = contents[CFG_PATH].decode()
520→    cfg_part_re = re.compile(
521→        r'<part id="(\d+)"[^>]*>(.*?)</part>', re.DOTALL
522→    )
523→    cfg_name_re = re.compile(r'<metadata key="name" value="([^"]+)"\s*/>')
524→    cfg_object_re = re.compile(
525→        r'(<object id="(\d+)"[^>]*>)(.*?)(</object>)', re.DOTALL
526→    )
527→    cfg_plate_re = re.compile(
528→        r'(<plate>)(.*?)(</plate>)', re.DOTALL
529→    )
530→
531→    # The CLI emits exactly one <object> in the assembled file; find it and
532→    # capture its part blocks.
533→    obj_match = cfg_object_re.search(cfg)
534→    if obj_match is None:
535→        raise RuntimeError(f"{proj_3mf}: no <object> in {CFG_PATH}")
536→    obj_open, obj_id_str, obj_body, obj_close = obj_match.groups()
537→    composite_obj_id = int(obj_id_str)
538→
539→    # Parse parts: each part has an id and a name; the name is the STL filename.
540→    parts: list[tuple[int, str, str]] = []  # (part_id, name, full_part_xml)
541→    for m in cfg_part_re.finditer(obj_body):
542→        part_id = int(m.group(1))
543→        part_xml = m.group(0)
544→        name_match = cfg_name_re.search(m.group(2))
545→        if name_match is None:
546→            raise RuntimeError(f"{proj_3mf}: <part id={part_id}> missing name")
547→        name = name_match.group(1)
548→        parts.append((part_id, name, part_xml))
549→
550→    # Group parts by specimen index. Order within each specimen: struts first
551→    # (extruder 1), cables second (extruder 2).
552→    spec_to_parts: dict[int, dict[int, tuple[int, str, str]]] = {}
553→    for part_id, name, part_xml in parts:
554→        if name not in name_to_spec:
555→            raise RuntimeError(
556→                f"{proj_3mf}: <part name={name!r}> not in pairs mapping"
557→            )
558→        spec_idx, ext_id = name_to_spec[name]
559→        spec_to_parts.setdefault(spec_idx, {})[ext_id] = (part_id, name, part_xml)
560→
561→    # Build the new <object> entries (one per specimen). Composite object IDs
562→    # start one past the original (to avoid collision with the part IDs which
563→    # are 1..len(parts)).
564→    new_composite_ids: list[int] = []
565→    cfg_new_objects: list[str] = []
566→    extruder_re = re.compile(r'(<metadata key="extruder" value=")\d+(")')
567→    for spec_idx in sorted(spec_to_parts):
568→        new_obj_id = composite_obj_id + spec_idx
569→        new_composite_ids.append(new_obj_id)
570→        chunks = [f'  <object id="{new_obj_id}">\n']
571→        chunks.append(f'    <metadata key="name" value="Specimen {spec_idx:02d}"/>\n')
572→        for ext_id in sorted(spec_to_parts[spec_idx]):
573→            _, _, part_xml = spec_to_parts[spec_idx][ext_id]
574→            # Force the correct extruder per part.
575→            if extruder_re.search(part_xml):
576→                part_xml = extruder_re.sub(rf"\g<1>{ext_id}\g<2>", part_xml)
577→            else:
578→                part_xml = part_xml.replace(
579→                    "</part>",
580→                    f'      <metadata key="extruder" value="{ext_id}"/>\n    </part>',
581→                )
582→            chunks.append("    " + part_xml + "\n")
583→        chunks.append("  </object>")
584→        cfg_new_objects.append("".join(chunks))
585→
586→    cfg_new_object_block = "\n".join(cfg_new_objects)
587→
588→    # Replace the single <object>...</object> block with the new ones.
589→    new_cfg = cfg[:obj_match.start()] + cfg_new_object_block + cfg[obj_match.end():]
590→
591→    # Patch <plate>: one <model_instance> per new composite.
592→    plate_match = cfg_plate_re.search(new_cfg)
593→    if plate_match is None:
594→        raise RuntimeError(f"{proj_3mf}: no <plate> in {CFG_PATH}")
595→    plate_open, plate_body, plate_close = plate_match.groups()
596→    plate_header_match = re.search(
597→        r'^(.*?)(<model_instance>.*?</model_instance>\s*)', plate_body, re.DOTALL
598→    )
599→    if plate_header_match is None:
600→        # No existing model_instance — just inject after a trailing <gcode_file>.
601→        plate_header = plate_body.rstrip() + "\n"
602→    else:
603→        plate_header = plate_header_match.group(1)
604→    new_instances: list[str] = []
605→    for i, new_obj_id in enumerate(new_composite_ids):
606→        new_instances.append(
607→            f'    <model_instance>\n'
608→            f'      <metadata key="object_id" value="{new_obj_id}"/>\n'
609→            f'      <metadata key="instance_id" value="0"/>\n'
610→            f'      <metadata key="identify_id" value="{100 + i}"/>\n'
611→            f'    </model_instance>\n'
612→        )
613→    new_plate = plate_open + plate_header + "".join(new_instances) + "  " + plate_close
614→    new_cfg = new_cfg[:plate_match.start()] + new_plate + new_cfg[plate_match.end():]
615→    contents[CFG_PATH] = new_cfg.encode()
616→
617→    # ---- Patch 3D/3dmodel.model next. -----------------------------------------
618→    model_xml = contents[MODEL_PATH].decode()
619→    model_obj_re = re.compile(
620→        r'(<object id="(\d+)"[^>]*type="model"[^>]*>)(.*?)(</object>)',
621→        re.DOTALL,
622→    )
623→    model_component_re = re.compile(
624→        r'<component\b[^>]*?objectid="(\d+)"[^>]*?/>'
625→    )
626→    model_build_re = re.compile(
627→        r'(<build[^>]*>)(.*?)(</build>)', re.DOTALL
628→    )
629→    model_item_re = re.compile(
630→        r'<item\b[^>]*?objectid="\d+"[^>]*?/>'
631→    )
632→
633→    obj_match2 = model_obj_re.search(model_xml)
634→    if obj_match2 is None:
635→        raise RuntimeError(f"{proj_3mf}: no <object type=model> in {MODEL_PATH}")
636→    obj_open2, _obj_id2, obj_body2, obj_close2 = obj_match2.groups()
637→    components = model_component_re.findall(obj_body2)
638→    # Capture the *full* component tags too (we want to preserve transforms).
639→    component_tags = re.findall(r'<component\b[^>]*?/>', obj_body2)
640→    if len(component_tags) != len(parts):
641→        raise RuntimeError(
642→            f"{proj_3mf}: {MODEL_PATH} has {len(component_tags)} components "
643→            f"but {CFG_PATH} has {len(parts)} parts"
644→        )
645→    # Build a mapping component objectid -> tag.
646→    obj_id_to_tag: dict[str, str] = {}
647→    for tag in component_tags:
648→        m = re.search(r'objectid="(\d+)"', tag)
649→        if m:
650→            obj_id_to_tag[m.group(1)] = tag
651→
652→    # Build new <object> entries. Each one wraps the two component tags for
653→    # that specimen (struts first, cables second, matching the order they
654→    # were passed to --assemble).
655→    new_model_objects: list[str] = []
656→    # Determine the (composite_id, [part_id, part_id]) layout to know
657→    # which underlying mesh objects belong to which specimen.
658→    for spec_idx in sorted(spec_to_parts):
659→        new_obj_id = composite_obj_id + spec_idx
660→        comp_tags: list[str] = []
661→        for ext_id in sorted(spec_to_parts[spec_idx]):
662→            part_id, _, _ = spec_to_parts[spec_idx][ext_id]
663→            tag = obj_id_to_tag.get(str(part_id))
664→            if tag is None:
665→                raise RuntimeError(
666→                    f"{proj_3mf}: no <component objectid={part_id}> in {MODEL_PATH}"
667→                )
668→            comp_tags.append("    " + tag)
669→        new_model_objects.append(
670→            f'  <object id="{new_obj_id}" p:UUID="{uuid.uuid4()}" type="model">\n'
671→            f'   <components>\n'
672→            + "\n".join(comp_tags) + "\n"
673→            f'   </components>\n'
674→            f'  </object>'
675→        )
676→    new_model_object_block = "\n".join(new_model_objects)
677→    new_model_xml = (
678→        model_xml[: obj_match2.start()]
679→        + new_model_object_block
680→        + model_xml[obj_match2.end() :]
681→    )
682→
683→    # Replace the single <item> in <build> with one <item> per new composite.
684→    build_match = model_build_re.search(new_model_xml)
685→    if build_match is None:
686→        raise RuntimeError(f"{proj_3mf}: no <build> in {MODEL_PATH}")
687→    build_open, build_body, build_close = build_match.groups()
688→    existing_item_match = model_item_re.search(build_body)
689→    if existing_item_match is None:
690→        raise RuntimeError(f"{proj_3mf}: no <item> in <build>")
691→    # Reuse the existing transform attribute so the plate placement stays.
692→    existing_item = existing_item_match.group(0)
693→    transform_match = re.search(r'transform="([^"]*)"', existing_item)
694→    printable_match = re.search(r'printable="([^"]*)"', existing_item)
695→    transform_attr = (
696→        f' transform="{transform_match.group(1)}"' if transform_match else ""
697→    )
698→    printable_attr = (
699→        f' printable="{printable_match.group(1)}"' if printable_match else ' printable="1"'
700→    )
701→    new_items: list[str] = []
702→    for new_obj_id in new_composite_ids:
703→        new_items.append(
704→            f'  <item objectid="{new_obj_id}" p:UUID="{uuid.uuid4()}"'
705→            f"{transform_attr}{printable_attr}/>"
706→        )
707→    new_build = build_open + "\n" + "\n".join(new_items) + "\n " + build_close
708→    new_model_xml = (
709→        new_model_xml[: build_match.start()] + new_build + new_model_xml[build_match.end() :]
710→    )
711→    contents[MODEL_PATH] = new_model_xml.encode()
712→
713→    # ---- Rewrite the archive ---------------------------------------------------
714→    with zipfile.ZipFile(proj_3mf, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zout:
715→        for info in infos:
716→            zout.writestr(info, contents[info.filename])
717→

719→def build_mm_3mf(
720→    pairs: list[tuple[Path, Path]], out_3mf: Path
721→) -> None:
722→    """Assemble per-specimen (struts, cables) STL pairs into a Bambu H2D MM ``.3mf``.
723→
724→    Each pair becomes its own composite object on the build plate with two
725→    parts (struts → extruder 1 / PLA, cables → extruder 2 / TPU), so each
726→    specimen can be moved as a unit in Bambu Studio while keeping the PLA
727→    and TPU members locked together (PR #35 comment 4513722886).
728→

833→    # ---- Sobol-only Ax client (no model / no eval) -------------------------
834→    # Ax's default GenerationStrategy starts with a Sobol init step, so a

864→            file=sys.stderr,

866→
867→    # ---- Persist the design table -----------------------------------------
868→    frozen = {

870→        "tiling": TILING,

872→        "build_orientation": BUILD_ORIENTATION,
873→        "tpu_shore": TPU_SHORE,
874→        "strut_material": STRUT_MATERIAL,
875→        "cable_material": CABLE_MATERIAL,

888→            )
889→    json_path.write_text(json.dumps(
890→        {
891→            "seed": args.seed,
892→            "n": args.n,
893→            "grid": {"rows": rows, "cols": cols, "cell_x": cell_x, "cell_y": cell_y},
894→            "plate": {"x_mm": PLATE_X, "y_mm": PLATE_Y, "margin_mm": PLATE_MARGIN,
895→                       "prime_tower_reserve_x_mm": PRIME_TOWER_RESERVE_X},
896→            "parameters": PARAMETERS,
897→            "frozen": frozen,
898→            "specimens": [{"idx": i, **s} for i, s in enumerate(specimens)],
899→        },

902→
903→    # ---- Render combined SCAD -> STL + PNG previews ------------------------

905→    if args.skip_render:

908→    if not shutil.which("openscad"):

910→              file=sys.stderr)
911→        return 2
912→
913→    print(f"==> OpenSCAD render -> {stl_path.name} (n={args.n} specimens on plate)")
914→    run_openscad(scad_path, stl_path)
915→    print(f"==> OpenSCAD render -> {stl_struts_path.name} (struts + joints only, extruder 1 / PLA)")
916→    run_openscad(scad_path, stl_struts_path, defines={"part": "struts"})

918→    run_openscad(scad_path, stl_cables_path, defines={"part": "cables"})

920→    # Per-specimen STLs (one struts + one cables STL per specimen) — the
921→    # BambuStudio --assemble step uses these to build one composite object
922→    # per specimen with two parts each (PR #35 comment 4513722886).
923→    per_spec_dir = out_dir / "per-specimen-stls"

1→"""Bridge from PR #30's BO campaign parameterization → MuJoCo Tier-C sim.
  2→
  3→This module is a *drop-in replacement* for the analytical
  4→``bo.tensegrity_campaign.simulate_specimen`` dummy evaluator.  It maps an
  5→Ax parameterization (the design-space dict that ``AxClient.get_next_trial``
  6→returns) to the three campaign objectives by running the existing Tier-C
  7→MuJoCo regime simulation in ``simulations.run_regimes``:
  8→
  9→    F_peak_N      — peak transmitted force = peak |a_z| (m/s²) × payload mass
 10→    SEA_J_per_g   — specific energy absorbed = max tendon strain energy / cell mass
 11→    eta           — compaction efficiency  = mean force / peak force over the
 12→                    pulse window (so a square plateau ≈ 1.0; a triangle ≈ 0.5)
 13→
 14→For each tier-C evaluation, we:
 15→  1. Convert the BO parameters into a
 16→     :class:`simulations.printable_design.PrintableDesign` and run
 17→     ``check()``; if the design is infeasible (class-2 strut overlap, tendon
 18→     unprintable, prestrain past TPU break, etc.) we return penalised
 19→     objectives so Ax learns the feasibility boundary cheaply.
 20→  2. Build an overridden :class:`simulations.regimes.Regime` whose tendon
 21→     stiffness, strut radius, prestrain, and cell scale match the BO
 22→     parameters; keep the regime's payload-mass + ΔV (so we are
 23→     *evaluating* the design against a fixed loading scenario, not changing
 24→     the loading along with the design).
 25→  3. Call :func:`simulations.run_regimes.simulate` for one trial.
 26→  4. Compute F_peak, SEA, eta from the returned time-series.
 27→
 28→Only the T3-prism topology is implemented; other PR #24/PR #30 topologies
 29→(truncated_octahedron, simplex_4_strut, stacked_prism) fall back to the
 30→T3 mesher and emit a warning so the BO loop can still propose them but
 31→their fitness reflects T3 physics.  This is exactly the scope @sgbaird
 32→called out in PR comment 4500844340: "we'll probably run simulations for
 33→each of samples from #30 beginning with a set of T3 structures (#35) that
 34→we've already been able to print."
 35→
 36→Both BO parameter schemas are accepted: the PR #30 scaffold
 37→(``strut_diameter_mm``/``strut_length_mm``/``cable_diameter_mm``/
 38→``twist_angle_deg``/``prestress_pct``) and the PR #35 T3-prism batch
 39→(``R_mm``/``H_mm``/``twist_deg``/``strut_d_mm``/``cable_d_mm`` from
 40→``bo/t3_prism_sobol_batch.py``).  See :func:`normalize_parameterization`.
 41→
 42→Multi-fidelity (Newton tier-B, PolyFEM tier-A) is stubbed by ``fidelity``
 43→keyword — future work, but the function signature is forward-compatible
 44→with Ax's ``MultiFidelityAcquisition`` (Frazier 2018).
 45→
 46→Usage in ``bo/tensegrity_campaign.py``::
 47→
 48→    from simulations.bo_evaluator import evaluate_design
 49→
 50→    response = evaluate_design(parameterization, regime=CRUTCH, fidelity="C")
 51→    # response = {"F_peak_N": float, "SEA_J_per_g": float, "eta": float}
 52→"""
 53→from __future__ import annotations
 54→
 55→import math
 56→import sys
 57→import warnings
 58→from dataclasses import replace
 59→from pathlib import Path
 60→from typing import Literal, Mapping
 61→
 62→# Make this script importable both as ``simulations.bo_evaluator`` *and*
 63→# directly (``python simulations/bo_evaluator.py``) regardless of CWD.
 64→_HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
 65→if str(_HERE) not in sys.path:
 66→    sys.path.insert(0, str(_HERE))
 67→
 68→import numpy as np
 69→
 70→from printable_design import (  # noqa: E402
 71→    EQUILIBRIUM_TWIST,
 72→    PLA,
 73→    PrintableDesign,
 74→    TPU85A,
 75→)
 76→from regimes import CRUTCH, NASA_LANDER, Regime  # noqa: E402
 77→
 78→# Map PR #30 ``tpu_shore`` choices to Young's modulus (MPa).  TPU 95A is
 79→# ~2× stiffer than 85A per unit cross-section.
 80→_TPU_E_MPA: Mapping[str, float] = {"85A": TPU85A.young_MPa, "95A": 25.0}
 81→
 82→# Penalty values returned for infeasible designs.  Chosen so they sit well
 83→# *outside* the Ax objective thresholds in ``bo/tensegrity_campaign.py``
 84→# (F_PEAK_THRESHOLD=2500 N, SEA_THRESHOLD=0.05 J/g, ETA_THRESHOLD=0.20),
 85→# which makes them automatically pruned from the Pareto front while still
 86→# being learnable as a boundary by the GP.
 87→_INFEASIBLE_F_PEAK_N = 5.0e4   # ~5 t — definitely crushes the user
 88→_INFEASIBLE_SEA_J_PER_G = 1.0e-6
 89→_INFEASIBLE_ETA = 1.0e-3
 90→
 91→
 92→def _topology_warning(topology: str) -> None:
 93→    if topology not in {"t3_prism", None}:
 94→        warnings.warn(
 95→            f"bo_evaluator: topology={topology!r} not yet implemented; "
 96→            "running T3-prism physics and flagging.  Per PR #35 the lab is "
 97→            "starting BO with T3-prism prints, so this is fine for the "
 98→            "first batch; revisit when topology mesher lands.",
 99→            stacklevel=2,
100→        )
101→
102→
103→# PR #35 (``bo/t3_prism_sobol_batch.py``) uses real-mm, post-scale T3-prism
104→# parameter names that differ from the PR #30 scaffold.  Map them onto the
105→# canonical PR #30 names so a single evaluator serves both campaigns.
106→_PR35_TO_PR30: Mapping[str, str] = {
107→    "R_mm": "cell_radius_mm",
108→    "H_mm": "strut_length_mm",
109→    "twist_deg": "twist_angle_deg",
110→    "strut_d_mm": "strut_diameter_mm",
111→    "cable_d_mm": "cable_diameter_mm",
112→}
113→
114→
115→def normalize_parameterization(params: Mapping) -> dict:
116→    """Return a copy of ``params`` keyed by the canonical PR #30 names.
117→
118→    Accepts either the PR #30 ``bo/tensegrity_campaign.py`` schema
119→    (``strut_diameter_mm``/``strut_length_mm``/``cable_diameter_mm``/
120→    ``twist_angle_deg``) *or* the PR #35 ``bo/t3_prism_sobol_batch.py``
121→    schema (``R_mm``/``H_mm``/``twist_deg``/``strut_d_mm``/``cable_d_mm``).
122→    PR #35 names take precedence when both are present.  For the PR #35
123→    schema ``H_mm`` is the full cell height and ``R_mm`` the circumscribing
124→    radius, so we map them straight onto the PrintableDesign geometry rather
125→    than the radius≈L/2 heuristic the PR #30 path falls back to.
126→
127→    Twist convention: the CAD/PR #35 strut connectivity is ``B_i → T_i`` with
128→    an equilibrium twist of 60° (``cad/t3-prism/t3-prism.scad``), whereas the
129→    simulator's :func:`tprism_geometry.tprism_nodes` uses ``B_i → T_{i+1}``
130→    with an equilibrium twist of 150°.  The two describe the *same* prism when
131→    ``sim_twist = scad_twist + 120°`` (the +120° accounts for the
132→    next-vertex strut connectivity), so a PR #35 ``twist_deg`` is offset by
133→    +120° as it is mapped onto the simulator's ``twist_angle_deg``.  Without
134→    this offset every printed T3-prism (PR #35 twist ∈ [40°, 80°]) would be
135→    mis-flagged class-2 because the struts appear to cross the central axis.
136→    """
137→    out = dict(params)
138→    for pr35, pr30 in _PR35_TO_PR30.items():
139→        if pr35 in params:
140→            value = float(params[pr35])
141→            if pr35 == "twist_deg":
142→                value += 120.0  # CAD (B_i→T_i) → sim (B_i→T_{i+1}) convention
143→            out[pr30] = value
144→    return out
145→
146→
147→def parameterization_to_design(params: Mapping) -> PrintableDesign:
148→    """Map an Ax ``parameterization`` dict → :class:`PrintableDesign`.
149→
150→    Only the geometric / printable axes from ``bo/tensegrity_campaign.py``
151→    (PR #30) or ``bo/t3_prism_sobol_batch.py`` (PR #35) are consumed here;
152→    the rest (tiling, infill pattern, build orientation) are honoured by the
153→    surrounding evaluator wrapper, not by the printable-design model.
154→    """
155→    params = normalize_parameterization(params)
156→    twist_rad = math.radians(float(params.get("twist_angle_deg",
157→                                              math.degrees(EQUILIBRIUM_TWIST))))
158→    height_m = float(params.get("strut_length_mm", 25.0)) * 1e-3
159→    # Circumscribing radius from the T-prism node coordinates: with the
160→    # default twist the strut-to-strut chord length is ~radius·√3, so for
161→    # a given strut length L the cell radius ≈ L / (√3 · (1 + cos(twist))).
162→    # In practice ``run_regimes`` carries its own radius_m; we anchor on
163→    # the regime's cell scale and only scale tendon stiffness.
164→    radius_m = float(params.get("cell_radius_mm",
165→                                params.get("strut_length_mm", 25.0) * 0.5)) * 1e-3
166→    return PrintableDesign(
167→        radius_m=radius_m,
168→        height_m=height_m,
169→        twist_rad=twist_rad,
170→        strut_diameter_m=float(params["strut_diameter_mm"]) * 1e-3,
171→        tendon_diameter_m=float(params["cable_diameter_mm"]) * 1e-3,
172→        prestrain=float(params.get("prestress_pct", 0.0)) / 100.0,
173→    )
174→
175→
176→def _t3_seed_designs() -> list[dict]:
177→    """Pre-printed T3 designs (PR #35) ready as the first BO batch.
178→
179→    These are the parameterizations the lab can drop in as ``existing_data``
180→    when the BO campaign turns on, so Ax has real observations from the
181→    designs we already have hardware for.  Expressed in the PR #35
182→    ``bo/t3_prism_sobol_batch.py`` schema (real mm, post-scale) so the cell
183→    geometry matches the printed parts exactly.
184→    """
185→    base = {
186→        "topology": "t3_prism",
187→        "tiling": "1x1x1",
188→        "tpu_shore": "85A",
189→        "build_orientation": "vertical",
190→        "struts_per_cell": 3,
191→    }
192→    return [
193→        # PR #35 production target (scale 1.5×): R=37.5, H=105, cable_d 4.5 mm
194→        {**base, "R_mm": 37.5, "H_mm": 105.0, "twist_deg": 60.0,
195→         "strut_d_mm": 9.0, "cable_d_mm": 4.5, "prestress_pct": 0.0},
196→        # PR #35 baseline (scale 1.0×): R=25, H=70, cable_d 3.0 mm
197→        {**base, "R_mm": 25.0, "H_mm": 70.0, "twist_deg": 60.0,
198→         "strut_d_mm": 6.0, "cable_d_mm": 3.0, "prestress_pct": 0.0},
199→        # High-twist / fat-cable corner of the PR #35 Sobol box
200→        {**base, "R_mm": 40.0, "H_mm": 110.0, "twist_deg": 80.0,
201→         "strut_d_mm": 12.0, "cable_d_mm": 5.5, "prestress_pct": 2.0},
202→    ]
203→
204→
205→def evaluate_design(
206→    parameterization: Mapping,
207→    *,
208→    regime: Regime = CRUTCH,
209→    fidelity: Literal["C", "B", "A"] = "C",
210→) -> dict[str, float]:
211→    """Run one simulation and return PR #30's three BO objectives.
212→
213→    Parameters
214→    ----------
215→    parameterization
216→        Ax parameter dict, schema = ``bo/tensegrity_campaign.PARAMETERS``.
217→    regime
218→        Loading scenario (CRUTCH or NASA_LANDER from
219→        ``simulations.regimes``).  Loading is *fixed* per BO campaign, not
220→        a design variable.
221→    fidelity
222→        "C" = MuJoCo (current default — cheap, ~1 s),
223→        "B" = Newton/Warp XPBD (planned, ~30 s),
224→        "A" = PolyFEM+IPC (planned, ~5 min).  Only "C" is implemented.
225→
226→    Returns
227→    -------
228→    dict with keys ``"F_peak_N"``, ``"SEA_J_per_g"``, ``"eta"`` matching
229→    the ``F_PEAK``/``SEA``/``ETA`` outcome names in
230→    ``bo/tensegrity_campaign.py``.  Returns *penalised* values if the
231→    design is infeasible (class-2 strut overlap, unprintable tendon,
232→    prestrain past TPU yield, etc.).
233→    """
234→    if fidelity != "C":
235→        raise NotImplementedError(
236→            "Only Tier-C (MuJoCo) is wired in `bo_evaluator.evaluate_design`. "
237→            "Tier-B (Newton) and Tier-A (PolyFEM+IPC) are planned but require "
238→            "the per-cell tprism_mesh.py + newton_drop.py / polyfem_drop.py "
239→            "wrappers to accept an arbitrary PrintableDesign first; see "
240→            "simulations/bo_integration.md for the planned signature."
241→        )
242→
243→    _topology_warning(parameterization.get("topology"))
244→
245→    params = normalize_parameterization(parameterization)
246→    design = parameterization_to_design(params)
247→    issues = design.check()
248→    if issues:
249→        warnings.warn(
250→            "bo_evaluator: infeasible design: " + "; ".join(issues),
251→            stacklevel=2,
252→        )
253→        return {
254→            "F_peak_N": _INFEASIBLE_F_PEAK_N,
255→            "SEA_J_per_g": _INFEASIBLE_SEA_J_PER_G,
256→            "eta": _INFEASIBLE_ETA,
257→        }
258→
259→    # Import lazily so this module remains importable even when mujoco is
260→    # not installed (e.g., for ``edison_client``-only environments).
261→    from run_regimes import simulate  # noqa: E402
262→
263→    overridden = replace(
264→        regime,
265→        radius_m=design.radius_m,
266→        height_m=design.height_m,
267→        strut_radius_m=design.strut_diameter_m * 0.5,
268→        cable_stiffness_Npm=float(design.cable_stiffness_Npm),
269→        cable_pretension_frac=float(design.prestrain),
270→    )
271→    res = simulate(overridden)
272→
273→    peak_g = res["peak_g"]
274→    if not np.isfinite(peak_g):
275→        return {
276→            "F_peak_N": _INFEASIBLE_F_PEAK_N,
277→            "SEA_J_per_g": _INFEASIBLE_SEA_J_PER_G,
278→            "eta": _INFEASIBLE_ETA,
279→        }
280→
281→    f_peak_N = peak_g * 9.81 * regime.payload_mass_kg
282→
283→    # Cell mass for SEA: 3 PLA struts + 9 TPU tendons (cell-only; payload
284→    # is excluded so SEA reflects design intent).
285→    n = design.nodes
286→    L_strut = float(np.linalg.norm(n[0] - n[1]))      # any STRUTS[0]
287→    v_strut = 3 * math.pi * (design.strut_diameter_m / 2) ** 2 * L_strut
288→    L_tendon = float(np.linalg.norm(n[0] - n[3]))     # vertical tendon
289→    v_tendon = 9 * math.pi * (design.tendon_diameter_m / 2) ** 2 * L_tendon
290→    cell_mass_g = (v_strut * PLA.density_kgm3
291→                   + v_tendon * TPU85A.density_kgm3) * 1000.0
292→    sea_J_per_g = (res["sea_Jpkg"] * regime.payload_mass_kg) / max(cell_mass_g,
293→                                                                   1e-6)
294→
295→    # Compaction efficiency: mean |a| over the half-peak pulse window
296→    # divided by the peak (1.0 = perfect rectangular plateau).
297→    az_g = np.abs(np.asarray(res["az_g"]))
298→    if az_g.size and peak_g > 0:
299→        above = az_g >= 0.5 * peak_g
300→        eta = float(az_g[above].mean() / peak_g) if above.any() else 0.0
301→    else:
302→        eta = 0.0
303→
304→    return {
305→        "F_peak_N": float(f_peak_N),
306→        "SEA_J_per_g": float(sea_J_per_g),
307→        "eta": float(eta),
308→    }
309→
310→
311→def evaluate_batch_csv(
312→    csv_path,
313→    *,
314→    regime: Regime = CRUTCH,
315→    fidelity: Literal["C", "B", "A"] = "C",
316→) -> list[dict]:
317→    """Evaluate every row of a PR #35 ``t3-prism-bo-batch.csv`` design batch.
318→
319→    The batch generator in ``bo/t3_prism_sobol_batch.py`` emits the Sobol
320→    design set but reports *no* objectives back to Ax.  This reads that CSV,
321→    runs the Tier-C sim for each specimen, and returns the design row merged
322→    with its ``{F_peak_N, SEA_J_per_g, eta}`` so the values can be attached to
323→    the AxClient (``attach_trial`` + ``complete_trial``) as a cheap simulated
324→    prior before the physical drops are run.
325→    """
326→    import csv as _csv
327→
328→    rows: list[dict] = []
329→    with open(csv_path, newline="") as fh:
330→        for raw in _csv.DictReader(fh):
331→            params = {k: v for k, v in raw.items() if v not in (None, "")}
332→            # Coerce the numeric design columns; leave categoricals as str.
333→            for key in ("R_mm", "H_mm", "twist_deg", "strut_d_mm",
334→                        "cable_d_mm", "strut_diameter_mm", "strut_length_mm",
335→                        "cable_diameter_mm", "twist_angle_deg", "prestress_pct"):
336→                if key in params:
337→                    try:
338→                        params[key] = float(params[key])
339→                    except (TypeError, ValueError):
340→                        pass
341→            obj = evaluate_design(params, regime=regime, fidelity=fidelity)
342→            rows.append({**raw, **obj})
343→    return rows
344→
345→
346→if __name__ == "__main__":
347→    import argparse
348→
349→    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
350→        description="Tier-C MuJoCo evaluator for the tensegrity BO campaign "
351→                    "(PR #30 / PR #35 schemas).")
352→    parser.add_argument(
353→        "--batch-csv", default=None,
354→        help="Path to a PR #35 t3-prism-bo-batch.csv; evaluate every row.")
355→    parser.add_argument(
356→        "--regime", choices=["crutch_tip", "nasa_lander"],
357→        default="crutch_tip", help="Fixed loading scenario.")
358→    args = parser.parse_args()
359→
360→    _regime = NASA_LANDER if args.regime == "nasa_lander" else CRUTCH
361→
362→    if args.batch_csv:
363→        results = evaluate_batch_csv(args.batch_csv, regime=_regime)
364→        for i, r in enumerate(results):
365→            print(f"row #{i}  F_peak={float(r['F_peak_N']):9.1f} N  "
366→                  f"SEA={float(r['SEA_J_per_g']):8.4f} J/g  "
367→                  f"eta={float(r['eta']):.3f}")
368→    else:
369→        # Smoke-test against the three PR #35 T3 seed designs.
370→        for i, p in enumerate(_t3_seed_designs()):
371→            try:
372→                r = evaluate_design(p, regime=_regime, fidelity="C")
373→                print(f"seed #{i}  F_peak={r['F_peak_N']:9.1f} N  "
374→                      f"SEA={r['SEA_J_per_g']:8.4f} J/g  eta={r['eta']:.3f}")
375→            except Exception as e:        # pragma: no cover - smoke test
376→                print(f"seed #{i}  FAILED: {e!r}")

1→"""Drive the MuJoCo prism through both application regimes (issue #18 +
  2→issues #14/#16), embedded inside the Lansmont M23 envelope (issue #28).
  3→
  4→For each regime we:
  5→  1. Build a MuJoCo MJCF where the T-prism sits between the floor and a
  6→     plate carrying the regime-specific payload mass; the plate starts at
  7→     a height that gives the regime impact velocity.
  8→  2. Step the dynamics, record the time-history of payload acceleration,
  9→     plate force on the prism, and tendon strain energy.
 10→  3. Sweep cable stiffness over two decades and recompute peak |a| (g),
 11→     pulse width FWHM, and specific energy absorbed (SEA).
 12→  4. Plot one time-history figure plus one stiffness-sweep figure per
 13→     regime.
 14→
 15→Outputs are written to ``simulations/outputs/`` next to the existing
 16→single-engine demo plots.
 17→"""
 18→from __future__ import annotations
 19→
 20→import os
 21→import textwrap
 22→
 23→import matplotlib
 24→
 25→matplotlib.use("Agg")
 26→import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
 27→import mujoco
 28→import numpy as np
 29→
 30→from regimes import CRUTCH, NASA_LANDER, M23, Regime
 31→from tprism_geometry import CABLES, STRUTS, tprism_nodes
 32→
 33→OUT_DIR = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "outputs")
 34→os.makedirs(OUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)
 35→
 36→G = 9.81  # m/s^2
 37→
 38→
 39→def build_xml(r: Regime, *, cable_stiffness: float | None = None) -> str:
 40→    """Build MJCF for regime ``r``.
 41→
 42→    The prism sits with a 1 mm ground clearance and is given an initial
 43→    downward velocity equal to the regime impact velocity (i.e. we start
 44→    "at the moment of release after free-fall"); the plate above carries
 45→    the regime payload mass with the same initial velocity so the unit
 46→    cell is loaded in compression as soon as the bottom struts contact
 47→    the floor.  This keeps the simulation window short and avoids
 48→    spending compute on the free-fall phase.
 49→    """
 50→    if cable_stiffness is None:
 51→        cable_stiffness = r.cable_stiffness_Npm
 52→
 53→    z0 = 0.001  # 1 mm ground clearance
 54→    nodes = tprism_nodes(radius=r.radius_m, height=r.height_m, z0=z0)
 55→
 56→    plate_size = max(r.radius_m * 1.2, 0.02)
 57→    plate_thickness = 0.01
 58→    plate_z = z0 + r.height_m + plate_thickness * 0.5
 59→
 60→    bodies, sites = [], []
 61→    for s_idx, (a, b) in enumerate(STRUTS):
 62→        pa, pb = nodes[a], nodes[b]
 63→        center = 0.5 * (pa + pb)
 64→        sa = pa - center
 65→        sb = pb - center
 66→        bodies.append(textwrap.dedent(f"""
 67→            <body name="strut{s_idx}" pos="{center[0]:.6f} {center[1]:.6f} {center[2]:.6f}">
 68→              <freejoint/>
 69→              <geom type="capsule"
 70→                    fromto="{sa[0]:.6f} {sa[1]:.6f} {sa[2]:.6f}
 71→                            {sb[0]:.6f} {sb[1]:.6f} {sb[2]:.6f}"
 72→                    size="{r.strut_radius_m:.5f}" density="{r.strut_density_kgm3:.1f}"
 73→                    rgba="0.2 0.4 0.9 1"/>
 74→              <site name="n{a}" pos="{sa[0]:.6f} {sa[1]:.6f} {sa[2]:.6f}" size="0.003"/>
 75→              <site name="n{b}" pos="{sb[0]:.6f} {sb[1]:.6f} {sb[2]:.6f}" size="0.003"/>
 76→            </body>
 77→        """))
 78→    # Plate body: total mass = payload mass.
 79→    bodies.append(textwrap.dedent(f"""
 80→        <body name="payload" pos="0 0 {plate_z:.6f}">
 81→          <freejoint/>
 82→          <geom type="box" size="{plate_size:.4f} {plate_size:.4f} {plate_thickness*0.5:.4f}"
 83→                mass="{r.payload_mass_kg:.4f}" rgba="0.6 0.6 0.6 1"/>
 84→        </body>
 85→    """))
 86→
 87→    tendons = []
 88→    for c_idx, (a, b) in enumerate(CABLES):
 89→        L0 = float(np.linalg.norm(nodes[a] - nodes[b]))
 90→        rest = (1.0 - r.cable_pretension_frac) * L0
 91→        tendons.append(textwrap.dedent(f"""
 92→            <spatial name="cable{c_idx}" range="0 {rest:.6f}"
 93→                     stiffness="{cable_stiffness:.2f}"
 94→                     damping="{r.cable_damping_Nspm:.2f}"
 95→                     rgba="0.9 0.2 0.2 1" width="0.0008">
 96→              <site site="n{a}"/>
 97→              <site site="n{b}"/>
 98→            </spatial>
 99→        """))
100→
101→    return f"""
102→    <mujoco model="{r.name}">
103→      <option gravity="0 0 -9.81" timestep="{r.sim_dt_s}" integrator="RK4"/>
104→      <worldbody>
105→        <geom name="floor" type="plane" size="2 2 0.1" rgba="0.85 0.85 0.85 1"/>
106→        {''.join(bodies)}
107→      </worldbody>
108→      <tendon>
109→        {''.join(tendons)}
110→      </tendon>
111→    </mujoco>
112→    """
113→
114→
115→def simulate(r: Regime, *, cable_stiffness: float | None = None) -> dict:
116→    """Run one drop and return time-histories and scalar metrics."""
117→    xml = build_xml(r, cable_stiffness=cable_stiffness)
118→    model = mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_string(xml)
119→    data = mujoco.MjData(model)
120→
121→    # Identify payload body (last in the list).
122→    payload_id = model.nbody - 1
123→    nsteps = int(r.sim_duration_s / model.opt.timestep)
124→    t = np.zeros(nsteps)
125→    payload_z = np.zeros(nsteps)
126→    payload_vz = np.zeros(nsteps)
127→    se = np.zeros(nsteps)
128→
129→    # Set the payload's initial *downward* velocity equal to the regime's
130→    # drop velocity, so we don't have to wait for it to fall.  This puts
131→    # the prism into compression at t=0 with the correct kinetic energy.
132→    # The prism struts likewise need v_z = -drop_velocity to ride along
133→    # with the payload (they are free bodies stacked between floor + plate
134→    # and otherwise would lag).
135→    for i in range(model.nbody):
136→        if i == 0:                       # world
137→            continue
138→        # qvel layout: 6 dof per free joint (3 lin + 3 ang).  Index 2 = z.
139→        addr = model.body_dofadr[i]
140→        data.qvel[addr + 2] = -r.drop_velocity_mps
141→
142→    L0 = model.tendon_lengthspring[:, 1].copy()
143→    kspring = model.tendon_stiffness.copy()
144→
145→    last_finite = nsteps
146→    for k in range(nsteps):
147→        mujoco.mj_step(model, data)
148→        t[k] = data.time
149→        payload_z[k] = data.xpos[payload_id, 2]
150→        payload_vz[k] = data.cvel[payload_id, 5]   # linear z velocity
151→        strain = np.maximum(data.ten_length - L0, 0.0)
152→        se[k] = float(0.5 * np.sum(kspring * strain ** 2))
153→        if (not np.isfinite(payload_z[k]) or not np.isfinite(payload_vz[k])
154→                or se[k] > 1e6 or se[k] < 0):
155→            last_finite = k
156→            break
157→
158→    # Truncate to the finite/sane window for downstream metrics.
159→    t = t[:last_finite]
160→    payload_z = payload_z[:last_finite]
161→    payload_vz = payload_vz[:last_finite]
162→    se = se[:last_finite]
163→    if len(t) < 5:
164→        return {"regime": r.name, "t": t, "az_g": np.zeros_like(t),
165→                "vz": payload_vz, "z": payload_z, "se": se,
166→                "peak_g": float("nan"), "pulse_ms": float("nan"),
167→                "sea_Jpkg": float("nan"),
168→                "cable_stiffness_Npm": float(model.tendon_stiffness[0])}
169→
170→    dt = model.opt.timestep
171→    az = np.gradient(payload_vz, dt)
172→    peak_g = float(np.max(np.abs(az)) / G)
173→    abs_a = np.abs(az) / G
174→    half = peak_g / 2.0
175→    above = abs_a >= half
176→    pulse_ms = (above.sum() * dt) * 1e3 if above.any() else 0.0
177→    sea = float(se.max() / r.payload_mass_kg)   # J/kg specific energy abs.
178→
179→    return {
180→        "regime": r.name,
181→        "t": t, "az_g": az / G, "vz": payload_vz, "z": payload_z, "se": se,
182→        "peak_g": peak_g, "pulse_ms": pulse_ms, "sea_Jpkg": sea,
183→        "cable_stiffness_Npm": float(model.tendon_stiffness[0]),
184→    }
185→
186→
187→def plot_timeseries(res_list: list[dict], regime: Regime, fname: str) -> None:
188→    fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 1, figsize=(7.5, 8), sharex=True)
189→    for res in res_list:
190→        lbl = f"k = {res['cable_stiffness_Npm']:.0f} N/m"
191→        axes[0].plot(res["t"] * 1e3, res["az_g"], label=lbl)
192→        axes[1].plot(res["t"] * 1e3, res["vz"], label=lbl)
193→        axes[2].plot(res["t"] * 1e3, res["se"], label=lbl)
194→    axes[0].axhline(regime.target_peak_g, ls="--", color="grey",
195→                    label=f"target ≤ {regime.target_peak_g:.0f} g")
196→    axes[0].axhline(-regime.target_peak_g, ls="--", color="grey")
197→    axes[0].set_ylabel("payload accel (g)")
198→    axes[0].set_title(f"{regime.name}: {regime.description}")
199→    axes[0].legend(fontsize=8, loc="upper right")
200→    axes[1].set_ylabel("payload v_z (m/s)")
201→    axes[2].set_ylabel("tendon strain E (J)")
202→    axes[2].set_xlabel("time (ms)")
203→    for ax in axes:
204→        ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
205→    fig.tight_layout()
206→    fig.savefig(os.path.join(OUT_DIR, fname), dpi=120)
207→    plt.close(fig)
208→
209→
210→def plot_sweep(rows: list[dict], regime: Regime, fname: str) -> None:
211→    ks = np.array([r["cable_stiffness_Npm"] for r in rows])
212→    pg = np.array([r["peak_g"] for r in rows])
213→    sea = np.array([r["sea_Jpkg"] for r in rows])
214→
215→    fig, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.5))
216→    color1 = "tab:red"
217→    ax1.set_xscale("log")
218→    ax1.plot(ks, pg, "o-", color=color1, label="peak |a| (g)")
219→    ax1.axhline(regime.target_peak_g, ls="--", color=color1, alpha=0.5,
220→                label=f"target ≤ {regime.target_peak_g:.0f} g")
221→    ax1.set_xlabel("cable (TPU tendon) stiffness (N/m)")
222→    ax1.set_ylabel("peak |payload accel| (g)", color=color1)
223→    ax1.tick_params(axis="y", labelcolor=color1)
224→    ax1.grid(True, which="both", alpha=0.3)
225→
226→    ax2 = ax1.twinx()
227→    color2 = "tab:blue"
228→    ax2.plot(ks, sea, "s--", color=color2, label="SEA (J/kg)")
229→    ax2.set_ylabel("specific energy absorbed (J/kg)", color=color2)
230→    ax2.tick_params(axis="y", labelcolor=color2)
231→
232→    ax1.set_title(f"{regime.name}: BO objective surface (1-D slice)")
233→    fig.tight_layout()
234→    fig.savefig(os.path.join(OUT_DIR, fname), dpi=120)
235→    plt.close(fig)
236→
237→
238→def main():
239→    print(f"Lansmont M23 envelope: {M23}\n")
240→    summary_rows = []
241→    for regime in (CRUTCH, NASA_LANDER):
242→        print(f"=== Regime: {regime.name} ===")
243→        print(f"   {regime.description}")
244→
245→        # 1. Three illustrative single runs (soft / nominal / stiff cable).
246→        ks_show = np.array([0.25, 1.0, 4.0]) * regime.cable_stiffness_Npm
247→        ts_runs = [simulate(regime, cable_stiffness=float(k)) for k in ks_show]
248→        plot_timeseries(ts_runs, regime,
249→                        f"regime_{regime.name}_timeseries.png")
250→        for res in ts_runs:
251→            print(f"   k={res['cable_stiffness_Npm']:8.0f} N/m  "
252→                  f"peak={res['peak_g']:7.1f} g  "
253→                  f"pulse={res['pulse_ms']:5.2f} ms  "
254→                  f"SEA={res['sea_Jpkg']:7.3f} J/kg")
255→
256→        # 2. Stiffness sweep for the BO-objective figure.
257→        ks_sweep = np.geomspace(0.05, 8.0, 11) * regime.cable_stiffness_Npm
258→        sweep_rows = [simulate(regime, cable_stiffness=float(k))
259→                      for k in ks_sweep]
260→        plot_sweep(sweep_rows, regime, f"regime_{regime.name}_sweep.png")
261→
262→        # 3. Save numeric summary CSV.
263→        arr = np.array([(s["cable_stiffness_Npm"], s["peak_g"],
264→                         s["pulse_ms"], s["sea_Jpkg"]) for s in sweep_rows])
265→        np.savetxt(os.path.join(OUT_DIR, f"regime_{regime.name}_sweep.csv"),
266→                   arr, delimiter=",",
267→                   header="cable_stiffness_Npm,peak_g,pulse_ms,sea_Jpkg",
268→                   comments="")
269→
270→        # 4. Pick the best-by-target row for the final summary.
271→        best = min(sweep_rows, key=lambda s: abs(s["peak_g"]
272→                                                 - regime.target_peak_g))
273→        summary_rows.append((regime.name, best))
274→        print(f"   best-fit-to-target: k={best['cable_stiffness_Npm']:.0f} N/m, "
275→              f"peak={best['peak_g']:.1f} g (target ≤ {regime.target_peak_g} g), "
276→              f"pulse={best['pulse_ms']:.2f} ms, SEA={best['sea_Jpkg']:.3f} J/kg\n")
277→
278→    print("== Summary ==")
279→    print(f"{'regime':<14} {'k* (N/m)':>10} {'peak (g)':>10} "
280→          f"{'pulse (ms)':>11} {'SEA (J/kg)':>11}")
281→    for name, b in summary_rows:
282→        print(f"{name:<14} {b['cable_stiffness_Npm']:>10.0f} "
283→              f"{b['peak_g']:>10.1f} {b['pulse_ms']:>11.2f} "
284→              f"{b['sea_Jpkg']:>11.3f}")
285→
286→
287→if __name__ == "__main__":
288→    main()

messages.content:
Here is a concise section-by-section summary of `manuscript-body.tex`:

---

## (1) What the paper is about
**Title:** "Bayesian Optimization of Multi-Material 3D-Printed Tensegrity-Inspired Structures for Energy Absorption"  
**Authors:** Jeffrey R. Hill & Sterling G. Baird (BYU), targeting ASME *Journal of Mechanical Design*.  
The paper presents an **experiment-driven BO framework** that trains a Gaussian-process surrogate directly on physical quasi-static compression and drop-weight impact data from multi-material FDM specimens (PLA struts + TPU tension elements) and uses it to recommend the next batch of tensegrity-inspired unit-cell designs to print and test. The closed-loop experimental campaign has **not yet produced reportable results** (manuscript is at the "planned-methods" phase).

---

## (2) BO Methods Explicitly Mentioned

| Method | Where |
|---|---|
| **Gaussian-process surrogate** (general BO) | Abstract, §Methods:BO, §Conclusions |
| **BoTorch / Ax** | §Intro (contribution 2), §Methods:BO, §Conclusions |
| **log-Expected Improvement (LogEI)** | §Methods:BO — "single-objective baseline" |
| **Noisy Expected Hypervolume Improvement (qNEHVI)** | §Methods:BO — "multi-objective case" |
| **Input-noise-robust acquisition** (Daulton et al. 2022) | §Methods:BO |
| **Evolution-guided constrained multi-objective BO** (Low et al. 2024) | §Methods:BO |
| **SAASBO** | §Methods:BO — "default acquisition pairing is SAASBO with qNEHVI" |
| **TuRBO** | §Methods:BO — planned escalation for high-dimensional tilings |
| **BOCS** (combinatorial baseline) | §Background:BO, §Methods:BO |
| **Mixed/categorical search spaces** (one-hot + rounded kernel) | §Background:BO, §Methods:BO |
| **Multifidelity BO** (Mo et al.) | §Background:BO, §Discussion — cited as prior art, not used here |
| **Co-Kriging / nonlinear information-fusion priors** (Perdikaris et al. 2017) | §Intro contribution 3 (TODO note) — under consideration for a future two-fidelity rung, not yet adopted |

**Kennedy-O'Hagan autoregressive co-kriging** and **MF-MES (multi-fidelity max-value entropy search)** are **not mentioned** anywhere in the manuscript.

---

## (3) BO-Related BibTeX Keys Cited

- `balandat2020botorch` — BoTorch (core implementation)
- `ament2023logei` — log-EI acquisition
- `daulton2021nehvi` — qNEHVI (noisy EHVI)
- `daulton2022robust` — input-noise-robust acquisition
- `low2024evolution` — evolution-guided constrained multi-objective BO
- `baptista2018bocs` — BOCS (combinatorial BO baseline)
- `garridomerchan2020dealingwithcategorical` — mixed/categorical search spaces
- `shahriari2016taking` — BO survey
- `frazier2018tutorial` — BO tutorial
- `mo2023accelerated` — multifidelity BO for architected materials (cited as prior art)
- `perdikaris2017nonlinear` — nonlinear information-fusion priors (cited in TODO for future co-Kriging)
- `wang2022bayesian`, `lee2023bayesian`, `zhang2021bo` — BO for metamaterial/AM design

---

## (4) Objective Formulation: Scalar vs. Pareto

**Both** are described:
- **Single-objective baseline:** LogEI maximizing SEA (or a single metric).
- **Multi-objective (Pareto):** qNEHVI simultaneously maximizing SEA and compaction efficiency $\eta_c$ while **constraining peak transmitted force** $F_{\max}$.  
- Metrics defined formally: $\mathrm{SEA} = \frac{1}{m}\int_0^{\delta_d} F(\delta)\,d\delta$ and $\eta_c = \frac{\int_0^{\delta_d} F(\delta)\,d\delta}{F_{\max}\,\delta_d}$.
- Results section has placeholder subsections for "Convergence of the BO Loop" and "**Pareto-Optimal Designs**" (Pareto front in peak-force vs. SEA space).

---

## (5) Tier-A/B/C Descriptions and Costs

**No explicit "Tier-A/B/C" terminology appears anywhere in the manuscript.** The closest analog is:
- A **two-fidelity escalation path** mentioned in §Intro contribution 3: (low-fidelity) direct experimental loop on FDM specimens → (higher-fidelity) pretensioned tensegrity assemblies with true cables and measured pretension for selected Pareto-optimal designs. No cost figures are given; the surrogate/fusion strategy is explicitly left open (TODO).
- A **higher-fidelity replicate campaign** on a Lansmont M23 drop tower + Polytec QTec laser vibrometry is planned for selected Pareto-optimal designs (§Methods:Testing).

---

## (6) Discrepancy Modeling Between Sim and Bench

**No discrepancy/bias modeling between simulation and bench is described.** The paper explicitly *avoids* simulation surrogates:
- §Background:BO: *"the present work shifts the emphasis from simulation surrogates to direct experimental data, appropriate for materials whose constitutive response is difficult to calibrate from first principles."*
- §Intro contribution 2: the BO loop "operates directly on physical … measurements … without requiring an accurate forward simulator."
- The co-Kriging / nonlinear-information-fusion option (Perdikaris 2017) is flagged in a TODO as a possible future addition once pretensioned-assembly data exist, but is not currently implemented.

---

## (7) PR #67 and PR #74 — Drop Tower and SAE J211 CFC-180

- **PR #67** is referenced in a `\todo` in §Methods:Testing (drop-weight impact paragraph):  
  > *"Cite the drop-test protocol document (PR #67) and the drop-test Edison LITERATURE\_HIGH brief (`653d7d39`) once integrated."*  
  It is associated with the **bungee-assisted laboratory drop tower protocol** (base accelerates faster than 1g, specimen constrained by light tethers, registered via transfer tape or V-block).

- **PR #74** is **not mentioned anywhere** in the manuscript body.

- **SAE J211 / CFC-180** is **not mentioned anywhere** in the manuscript body.
